history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration review and update the relevant policy documents to better clarify the credit rating criteria for foreign currency exchange counterparties.
history.administration_response: Work is ongoing to align the minimum long-term credit rating criteria for forward transaction counterparties with the minimum long-term credit-rating criteria for general foreign exchange (spot transaction) counterparties by updating the United Nations foreign currency hedging and budget rate-setting guidelines. The short-term credit-rating criteria are already aligned and the change to the minimum long-term credit-rating criteria will not affect the foreign exchange counterparties that the United Nations uses for forward transactions. For these forward transaction counterparties, the United Nations has International Swaps and Derivatives Association agreements in place with the counterparties that it uses. These agreements provide a standardized set of terms and conditions for derivatives, thereby ensuring certainty and consistency, as well as clear procedures for terminating and closing out transactions in the event of a default or other termination event, which can help to further mitigate counterparty credit risk.
history.board_assessment: Given that the relevant work is ongoing, the Board considers the recommendation to be under implementation.

history.sg_progress: The Administration is working to align the minimum long-term credit rating criteria for forward transaction counterparties with those applied to general foreign exchange (spot transaction) counterparties. This alignment will be achieved through updates to the United Nations foreign currency hedging and budget rate setting guidelines. The short-term credit rating criteria are already harmonized, and the proposed adjustment to the long-term criteria will not affect the current roster of forward transaction counterparties utilized by the Organization. For forward transactions, the United Nation maintains the International Swaps and Derivatives Association agreements with its counterparties. These agreements establish standardized terms and conditions for derivative transactions, ensuring consistency and legal certainty. They also include clearly defined close-out procedures, which facilitate the orderly termination of transactions in the event of default or other triggering events, thereby further mitigating counterparty credit risk.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration review and update the relevant policy documents to better clarify the credit rating criteria for foreign currency exchange counterparties.
history.administration_response: The recommendation was implemented. The Administration has updated and approved the United Nations foreign exchange policy and the United Nations foreign currency hedging and budget rate-setting guidelines to implement the Board’s recommendation. The three issues identified by the Board have been addressed: (a) the minimum rating requirements for forward transaction counterparties have been aligned with those for overall foreign exchange counterparties at A-, A3; (b) the previous wording that might have been taken to imply a priority among credit rating agencies has been removed and counterparties are now required to meet the minimum rating requirements from at least two credit rating agencies; and (c) the hedging guidelines now refer to all three credit rating agencies, consistent with the foreign exchange policy.
history.board_assessment: Given that all the issues identified by the Board have been addressed in the updated and approved policies, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
